name: Mineral water
anchor: strictest applicable sovereign drinking-water or packaged-water maximum, per litre of finished product as consumed, with the natural-mineral-water product-form split preserved as the governments write it
cross_reference: A naturally carbonated natural mineral water is governed by THIS row, not by the sparkling/carbonated-water row: its legal product form, not its carbonation, determines the applicable instrument. Mineralised or mineral-fortified purified water is not natural mineral water and routes to the bottled-drinking-water row.
native_basis_label: as consumed, per litre of natural mineral water in its packaged state (µg/L; numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
scope_note: In scope: natural mineral water as defined by the recognising authority — water from a protected underground source, bottled at source, of consistent characterising mineral composition, sold without treatment beyond those the instrument permits. This is a legally distinct product form, not a marketing label, and it is the one row of this category where the packaged-water bridge is partly switched off: EU Directive 2020/2184 expressly excludes natural mineral waters recognised under Directive 2009/54/EC from its scope, so no Drinking Water Directive value is used here. The instruments that do reach this form are FDA 21 CFR 165.110 (US law defines mineral water as a type of bottled water at s.165.110(a)(2)(iii), so the standards of quality apply, save that mineral water is exempt from the aesthetically based secondary levels) and the dedicated natural-mineral-water lines of Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, India FSSAI 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, GSO 193/2021, Colombia Res 4506/2013, Chile Decreto 977/1996 and Fiji FSR 2009. Where those instruments write a product-form split it is preserved rather than smoothed: total chromium is 50 µg/L here against 25 µg/L for other packaged drinking water, and nickel is 20 µg/L here against Hong Kong's 70 µg/L for other packaged drinking water. Out of scope: mineral-fortified or mineralised purified water, which is not natural mineral water and routes to the bottled-drinking-water row or, if flavoured, to Category 5; nothing on the basis of carbonation alone — a naturally carbonated natural mineral water stays on this row.
basis_guard: ^(?!.*(dry weight|dry matter|dehydrated|migration|leach|material content|surface|\bfeed\b|fat basis))(?=.*(water|as[ _]?consumed|mg/l|placed on market|food as listed)).*$
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a dietary per-litre / as-consumed water or food-schedule basis. The guard rejects dry-weight, dehydrated, migration/leachate, article material-content and feed bases outright, so a dry-commodity maximum level or a food-contact migration limit can never anchor a per-litre water cell. It admits mg/kg-expressed food-schedule rows (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011) because potable water density is within 0.3 per cent of 1 kg/L, so µg/kg and µg/L are the same number to well inside analytical uncertainty; that is a stated identity, not a silent conversion.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; strictest applicable sovereign maximum for the exact packaged-water form in its native per-litre as-consumed basis, disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, control where no defensible sovereign number exists; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Pb.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum for natural mineral water (FDA 21 CFR 165.110, which covers mineral water as a defined bottled-water type)
Pb.substantiation: Lead at 5 µg/L is compelled by FDA 21 CFR 165.110: in US law mineral water is a defined type of bottled water (s.165.110(a)(2)(iii)) and the standards of quality apply to it, so the 0.005 mg/L allowable level is a direct maximum for this product form, not a read-across. It is matched by the Health Canada maximum acceptable concentration and the NHMRC health-based guideline value under the packaged-water bridge. Every mineral-water-specific line in the pool is looser at 10 µg/L (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, India FSSAI 2016, GSO 193/2021, Colombia Res 4506/2013, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011) or 50 µg/L (Fiji FSR 2009); all are named and none is selected. The EU Drinking Water Directive value is not used on this row because the Directive excludes natural mineral water from its scope.

Cd.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Cd.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum (NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines health-based guideline value)
Cd.substantiation: Cadmium at 2 µg/L is the NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines health-based guideline value (0.002 mg/L), the strictest cadmium maximum any government sets for water. It is applied under the packaged-water bridge stated in the category method note: the product is the same substance in the same per-litre as-consumed basis, and the guideline carries no packaged-product carve-out. The next tier is 3 µg/L (WHO, Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, GSO 193/2021, Colombia Res 4506/2013), then 5 µg/L (EU Drinking Water Directive, FDA 21 CFR 165.110, EPA MCL, California), then 7 µg/L (Health Canada). All are named in the candidate set; none is selected because 2 µg/L is applicable and stricter. The mineral-water-specific lines cluster at 3 µg/L (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, India FSSAI 2016, GSO 193/2021, Colombia Res 4506/2013, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011) and are named in the candidate set. Cadmium is a contaminant, not a characterising mineral constituent, so nothing in the natural-mineral-water product definition makes the stricter drinking-water value inapplicable.

tAs.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
tAs.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum for natural mineral water (Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 item 2, natural-mineral-waters line)
tAs.substantiation: Total arsenic at 10 µg/L is unanimous across every mineral-water-specific line in the pool (Hong Kong Cap 132V, India FSSAI 2016, GSO 193/2021, Colombia Res 4506/2013, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, Israel FCS 2016) and across the packaged-water and drinking-water instruments that reach this form (FDA 21 CFR 165.110, NHMRC, Health Canada, WHO). Only Fiji is looser at 50 µg/L. There is no stricter sovereign total-arsenic value for mineral water anywhere in the register.

iAs.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
iAs.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum for the exact product form (Israel FCS 2016 row 16.1, whose scope names mineral water expressly)
iAs.substantiation: Inorganic arsenic at 6 µg/L is the Israel FCS 2016 maximum level for the exact product form ('Bottled drinking water and mineral water', source row 16.1, 0.006 mg/kg), the strictest sovereign inorganic-arsenic maximum for packaged water in the register. The alternatives are the US EPA drinking-water MCL recorded as inorganic arsenic at 10 µg/L and the Chilean Decreto 977/1996 Article 160 value of 10 µg/L for mineral and packaged drinking waters; both are named and neither is selected because 6 µg/L is applicable and stricter. The species cell is retained separately from total arsenic even though arsenic in potable water is effectively all inorganic, because the HMTc panel never allows a species to satisfy a total: a lot must clear both 10 µg/L total arsenic and 6 µg/L inorganic arsenic. Both named alternatives reach mineral water expressly: the Chilean value covers 'aguas minerales y aguas envasadas para bebida' and the EPA MCL reaches bottled mineral water through the FDA incorporation.

tHg.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
tHg.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum for natural mineral water (Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 item 12, natural-mineral-waters line)
tHg.substantiation: Total mercury at 1 µg/L is set for the exact product form by Hong Kong Cap 132V, India FSSAI 2016, GSO 193/2021, Colombia Res 4506/2013, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011 and Israel FCS 2016, and is matched by the NHMRC and Health Canada drinking-water values. The looser candidates are FDA 21 CFR 165.110 and Fiji FSR 2009 at 2 µg/L; both are named and neither is selected. Total mercury is published as a total and is never satisfied by a methylmercury or inorganic-mercury result.

MeHg.rationale: Mercury in sealed packaged drinking water is present essentially as inorganic Hg(II). Methylation is a microbial process requiring anaerobic sulfate- or iron-reducing activity in sediment or biota; it does not occur in a treated, filtered, disinfected and sealed packaged-water matrix, and there is no aquatic food chain in the product to bioaccumulate methylmercury. Methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury, so it is bounded by identity at the published total-mercury ceiling of 1 µg/L. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: Methylmercury is not separately quantified as a routine cell. Total mercury is measured on every certification lot by cold-vapour atomic fluorescence or ICP-MS against the published total-mercury ceiling. Where a lot result reaches or exceeds half the total-mercury ceiling, speciation by GC-ICP-MS or HPLC-ICP-MS is run as a reflex and the source water is investigated; a detectable methyl fraction is an immediate non-conformance regardless of the total-mercury result.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury maximum for drinking water, bottled water or natural mineral water. Every drinking-water and packaged-water instrument in the pool regulates mercury as total mercury with no methyl line, and Hong Kong Cap 132V regulates the packaged-drinking-water mercury cell as INORGANIC mercury (0.006 mg/kg, hk_cap132v_ihg_bottled-or-packaged-drinking-waters-other-than-natural_6), which is direct sovereign confirmation that the regulated mercury species in packaged water is the inorganic one. The only methylmercury maxima anywhere in the register are fish and aquatic-animal limits (for example fda_cpg540600_mehg_fish_1000), which govern a bioaccumulating tissue matrix and have no application to water.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU Directive 2020/2184 Annex I; EU Commission Directive 2003/40/EC (natural mineral waters); US EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations; US FDA 21 CFR 165.110; California SWRCB Title 22 s.64431; Health Canada Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality (2025 summary tables); NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines; WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality; Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2; Israel FCS 2016; India FSSAI 2016; Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011; GSO 193/2021; Colombia Res 4506/2013; Chile Decreto 977/1996; Fiji FSR 2009.

Ni.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Ni.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum for natural mineral water (Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 item 14, natural-mineral-waters line)
Ni.substantiation: Nickel at 20 µg/L is the Hong Kong Cap 132V maximum for the exact product form, matched by the NHMRC health-based guideline value. Hong Kong writes a product-form split here that runs the other way from the usual pattern: 20 µg/L for natural mineral waters against 70 µg/L for other packaged drinking waters, reflecting that a natural mineral water is bottled at source without the treatment stages that can add nickel. The looser candidates (WHO 70 µg/L; FDA 21 CFR 165.110 and California at 100 µg/L, both descending from the EPA nickel MCL remanded in 1995) are named and not selected. The EU Drinking Water Directive value of 20 µg/L is not used on this row because the Directive excludes natural mineral water, but it corroborates the number.

Sn.rationale: No sovereign sets a tin maximum for drinking water, bottled water or natural mineral water. The drinking-water instrument family carries no tin parameter at all (EU Directive 2020/2184 Annex I Parts B and C; US EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations; US FDA 21 CFR 165.110 standards of quality; Health Canada; NHMRC; WHO), and none of the national food-schedule packaged-water lines (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, India FSSAI 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, GSO 193/2021, Colombia Res 4506/2013, Chile Decreto 977/1996, Fiji FSR 2009) carries a tin entry for water. A read-across is not supportable: the nearest sovereign tin maxima are the canned-food and canned-beverage maximum levels, which exist to bound dissolution of tin from a tinplate container wall into an acidic canned matrix, and the canned-beverage value (100 mg/kg inorganic tin) sits roughly four orders of magnitude above anything a packaged water can plausibly contain, so importing it would publish a ceiling that functions as no limit at all. The dominant packaging for this category (PET, HDPE, glass, aluminium) contains no tin. Natural mineral water is bottled at source in glass or PET; tinplate presentation does not occur in this form. Tin therefore remains a mandatory control cell; no number is invented.
Sn.reference_method: Tin by ICP-MS on the finished packaged product in its native per-litre as-consumed basis, on every certification lot, reported against the method limit of quantification rather than a ceiling. Any quantifiable tin result triggers investigation of the container, closure and liner, the filling line and the source water, and lot release is withheld pending root-cause identification and a clean re-test. Where the product is presented in a tinplate or tin-coated container, the EU canned-beverage inorganic-tin maximum level recorded as the companion instrument applies as a regulatory hard stop in addition to this control.

Al.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Al.label: disclosed read-across from the packaged-drinking-water aluminium parameter; no government sets a direct aluminium maximum for natural mineral water
Al.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated, and that is verifiable from the instruments' own text rather than from silence: FDA 21 CFR 165.110 sets aluminium only as a secondary, aesthetically based allowable level and expressly EXEMPTS mineral water from aesthetically based allowable levels; EU Directive 2020/2184, whose Annex I Part C indicator parameter is 200 µg/L, excludes natural mineral water from its scope; and the EU instrument that does govern natural mineral water, Commission Directive 2003/40/EC, sets no aluminium value at all. The nearest applicable sovereign value is therefore the 200 µg/L packaged-drinking-water aluminium parameter, read across here and matched independently by the NHMRC aesthetic guideline of 200 µg/L. The alternatives that could have been read across are far looser (California 1000 µg/L; Health Canada 2900 µg/L), so this is the strictest supportable analog, not a convenient one. As on the other rows, 200 µg/L is an indicator / secondary / aesthetic parameter and is labelled as such rather than presented as a toxicological line.

Cr.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Cr.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum for natural mineral water (Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 item 7, natural-mineral-waters line)
Cr.substantiation: Total chromium at 50 µg/L for natural mineral water is the Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 item 7 maximum for the exact product form, matched by Health Canada, the WHO guideline value and the California MCL. The EU Drinking Water Directive value of 25 µg/L is NOT applied to this row: Directive 2020/2184 expressly excludes natural mineral waters recognised under Directive 2009/54/EC from its scope, so 25 µg/L is not an applicable maximum for this product form. That is a product-form split written by the government rule itself, and the method requires it to be preserved rather than smoothed away. The applicable EU instrument for natural mineral water is Commission Directive 2003/40/EC, which is absent from the register and is logged as a register gap; its chromium value of 50 µg/L is consistent with the Hong Kong anchor selected here. Published as a firm limit for the reason given on the other rows of this category.

Cr-VI.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Cr-VI.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum (California SWRCB Title 22 s.64431 Table 64431-A)
Cr-VI.substantiation: Hexavalent chromium at 10 µg/L is the California State Water Resources Control Board Title 22 section 64431 Table 64431-A maximum contaminant level (0.01 mg/L), re-adopted in 2024 after health-risk and feasibility analysis. It is the only enforceable hexavalent-chromium drinking-water maximum set by any government in the register; the sole alternative is the NHMRC guideline that hexavalent chromium should not exceed 50 µg/L, which is named and not selected. California is a sub-national government, so the selection is disclosed as such: it is adopted because it is a binding, enforceable governmental maximum for the same substance in the same basis and because it is the strictest applicable, not because it is federal. HMTc publishes Cr-VI as its own cell in addition to total chromium; a hexavalent result never satisfies the total-chromium cell and a total-chromium result never satisfies this one. Neither named instrument carves natural mineral water out of its scope.
